links.comparator_used: Conventional radiologist interpretation without AI (historical period); stand-alone AI output also evaluated
links.outcome: Radiologist diagnostic performance for lung metastasis on chest CT in colorectal cancer, with radiologists deciding whether to report AI-detected nodules
links.effect: Sensitivity 72.4% vs 32.1% (p = .008); accuracy 98.5% vs 96.0% (p = .005); management changes 55.2% vs 25.0% (p = .02); specificity 99.7% vs 98.9% (p = .11, ns); diagnostic yield 3.2% vs 1.4% (p = .30, ns); false-referral rate 0.3% vs 1.1% (p = .10, ns). Stand-alone AI had 381 false-positive detections in 634 patients without metastasis, and only one was reported as positive by radiologists.
links.tradeoff: Stand-alone AI produced many false positives (381 in 634 patients without metastasis), so radiologist filtering was needed. No significant change in specificity or false-referral rate was seen with AI assistance.
links.quote: AI assistance yielded increased sensitivity, accuracy, and frequency of management changes, without significantly changed specificity.

design_hint: AI-assisted radiologist interpretation with clinician discretion over AI-detected nodules
